content:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT created 2026-03-15T10:20:32Z (ts: 1938765432) — Paged KV cache metadata growth detected in prod-us-west-2. Symptoms: elevated block_manager.memory_rss, frequent paging spikes, increased tail latency for small-gen workloads. Initial severity: SEV-2. Automated trigger: kv_meta_count > 5M for 3m.

mike_s: noticing continuous-batching queue length jumps correlated with metadata growth. stack traces show block_manager hitting eviction loop frequently. Not yet widespread 503s but tail p95/p99 token latencies up ~3-4x for some routes.

julia_chen: looking at metrics now — block_meta_count went from ~1.1M -> 5.8M in ~6m. Eviction ops/sec spiked, and we see long GC pauses in the block manager logs. Links: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kv/kv-block-manager?panelId=3&orgId=1

sean_ops: confirmed one enterprise customer (org: atlas-pay) reported higher inference errors and few timeouts. Support ticket #24567 opened. No PII exposed.

priya_r: adding context — we rolled continuous-batching config change (PR #8421) yesterday to lower per-request batching latency; possible regression in how we compact metadata during aggressive batching.

mike_s: quick triage checklist:
- disable aggressive batching window (temp revert)
- bump eviction-aggressiveness to higher value to force more frequent evictions
- restart block-manager shards on affected nodes (rolling)
- patch to prevent metadata double-counting in paged-kv

julia_chen: trying safe action 1 — PATCH: set config `continuous_batch.window_ms = 10 -> 30` for prod-us-west-2 on the routing policy. Applying now via ops-console.

deploy-bot: deploy started by julia_chen: change continuous_batch.window_ms=30 to routing policy prod-us-west-2. CI: green. Instance groups: runtime-kgp-*-usw2.

mike_s: monitoring, creating a quick script to surface top keys with high metadata refs:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
curl -sS http://internal-kv-metrics:9100/metrics | grep block_meta | sort -nrk2 | head -n 30
```
sharing output in #eng-runtime infra. first pass shows certain long-running convo sessions and a few malformed requests causing repeated prefix writes.

sean_ops: started rolling restart of block-manager service on 6 nodes (staggered 60s). Will monitor error budget.

priya_r: creating emergency PR to fix double-counting in block header accounting: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8469 — adds idempotency guard when writing block metadata. Requesting hotfix backport to 2.3.x.

julia_chen: after config change + first node restarts, block_meta_count trend has flattened (5.8M -> 4.9M) and eviction ops/sec decreased. p95 latency for small-gen routes down ~30% from peak. Still watching p99.

mike_s: starting targeted cache compaction on a few noisy tenants: `curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kv/compact?tenant=atlas-pay` — executing with rate limit.

deploy-bot: hotfix branch `hotfix/kv-meta-idempotency` built and staged.

oncall-bot: NOTE: customer impact flagged for atlas-pay. Severity remains SEV-2 pending stabilization. Pager duty notified.

sean_ops: we saw one node with orphaned block refs due to interrupted compaction; manually reclaimed ~12GB of metadata on that node. Observability graphs show memory returning.

mike_s: mitigation summary so far:
- reverted aggressive batching window (prod routing policy) -> immediate improvement
- rolling restarts + targeted compaction -> reduced block_meta_count
- emergency hotfix PR -> prevents recurrence on write path
- increased eviction aggressiveness temporarily (config change)

julia_chen: next actions: PR review + backport to 2.3.x (priya), schedule graceful restart of remaining shards after hotfix lands (sean), monitor for 1h pre close.

priya_r: PR #8469 backport created: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8472. Requesting ops approval to cherry-pick and deploy to canary (2 nodes) before full roll.

sean_ops: canary deploy scheduled in 10m. Will watch for regen of block_meta_count or new errors.

mike_s: note for postmortem — collects: last batching change (PR #8421), compaction logs, block-manager evict cycle traces, tenant-specific noisy request patterns, monitoring dashboard snapshots. Will open postmortem ticket after incident stabilized.

julia_chen: canary good after 12m. No regression in canary nodes. Proceeding with gradual rollout to remaining nodes.

sean_ops: rollout complete. block_meta_count trending down to ~2.2M baseline. tail latency back within SLO for most routes.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT update: severity downgraded to SEV-3 at 1938765660. Customer impact reduced.

priya_r: filing emergency changelog and notes for release: highlights hotfix and recommended batching defaults.

mike_s: handing off to julia_chen for follow-up and postmortem write-up. julia_chen takes ownership. @julia_chen please confirm you got the handoff. :handshake:

julia_chen: got it — will draft postmortem and include timeline + long-term fixes (safer batching rollout gating, additional metrics for early detection, automated compaction triggers, block_manager memory caps). Will ping when draft ready.

sean_ops: leaving oncall notes in ops-runbook: increased eviction_aggressiveness is temporary; revert to baseline after 48h if stable.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT resolved? No — status: monitoring. last update: 1938765852.

mike_s: recording customer follow-up: reached out to atlas-pay support lead, provided incident summary and mitigation steps. No credit requested yet.

julia_chen: thanks everyone for quick response. I'll post the postmortem draft in ~24h and tag product/support for customer comms.

deploy-bot: deploy logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/builds/8469 (hotfix), https://ci.redwood/internal/builds/8472 (backport)

oncall-bot: thread closed for active mitigation handoffs. If metrics re-escalate, reopen thread or create new incident.
